articles.title: The Best Country Homes and Getaways in the UK for a Late Summer Staycation:
articles.description: English country-house escapes are two-a-penny these days — one need only place a toe outside a major city to be within spitting distance of a roaring fire and an extensive afternoon-tea menu — but none quite hits the spot like historic Cliveden House. Built in 1666 by the 2nd Duke of Buckingham, the soaring Palladian mansion overlooks some 376 acres of Buckinghamshire countryside, and you can revel in the extraordinary history of the house while, well, taking afternoon tea in front of the fire. You’d be in glamorous company, too: Cliveden, after all, is where Christine Keeler first met John Profumo, thus igniting the greatest scandal in British political history; it was used as a location in The Beatles’ movie Help; and the Duchess of Sussex checked in here the night before her wedding.
